display.title: Episode 418: Little Avraham Searches for Hashem (Mishenichnas Adar)
display.summary_short: Uncle Yossi welcomes the month of Adar with extra simcha, teaches what to think when saying the Shema, and tells how young Avraham discovered the one Creator.
display.summary_long: Broadcast on 2 Adar 5750. Uncle Yossi opens with the teaching that when Adar arrives we increase our simcha, serving Hashem with joy and getting a head start toward Purim, and the greatest simcha of all, the coming of Moshiach. After the Hakochainik march, a yeshiva student in Studio 604 leads the Shema. Mitzvah Time explains the meaning of the Shema's words: Shema means both listen and understand, Elokeinu means our God and also our strength and life, and the letters of Echad show that Hashem rules over the heavens, the earth and all four directions. A young listener answers questions about the Shema in a recorded phone call, and everyone gives tzedakah together. Story time tells how little Avraham, at three years old, looked at the sun, the moon and the stars and realized that none of them could be G-d, until he understood that there is one invisible Creator of everything. The show closes with a yahrzeit dedication, Shabbos candle-lighting time and a farewell.
display.lesson: Serve Hashem with extra joy in Adar, and when you say the Shema, think that Hashem is our God, our strength and our life, the one Creator of everything.

date.note: Dedication says the yahrzeit is 'today, Beis Adar'; 2 Adar 5750 was Tuesday 27 Feb 1990, matching the weekly estimate.
